mechanism: Counter = wall positions (cells k with c[k-1]==c[k]) to the right of the bell; the bell and the grid shift drop out. Each bounce is an Inc of the counter: if the first wall p1 is 1 or 2 it moves one cell right, and two walls that meet cancel (Gap-Inc). If p1 = 2j+1 is odd, the counter is 0 (10)^j W: a junction, i.e. a sub-bell of size j-1 for the counter W on the other grid. The carry then runs one complete phase of the machine itself on (j-1, W) and leaves 00 (10)^M' C', the sub-bell returned as an aligned d=1 frame followed by the sub-phase's new counter (J-rule; for j=1 this is the ordinary d=3 carry and the overflow). Phase(M, C) = M-1 Incs, then the marker walk (round-1 rules C1a/Z-absorb, C3a/C3b, C2, T; a frame with odd p1 is crossed by the J-rule with b=0). So the dynamics is a recursive phase map. On the orbit, every phase start is a one-junction counter G1 = (aligned prefix)(junction head)(aligned W). Every sub-phase runs on an aligned W. After the M-1 Incs the counter is fully aligned, so the walk uses only the round-1 aligned rules. Halting can only enter if M-1 < k_align(C), the number of Incs needed to resolve the junction chain.
notation: Counter C = cells after the bell (10)^M, starting at an even cell; walls p0=0<p1<p2<..., with a wall at every cell of the zero tail. Aligned frame (d,e) = walls at 0 and d, next frame at 2e+4 (round-1 blocks: d=1 'o S^(e+1)', d=2 'Z S^(e+1)', d=3 'Z o S^e'); terminator 'Z' = frame (3, width 4) before the tail; tail = endless width-2 frames 'o'. Junction = first gap odd >= 3 (cells 0 (10)^j, j >= 1). A = aligned: every frame wide (p1 in {1,2,3}, p2 even >= 4) up to the tail. G1 = A, or (wide aligned prefix) X W with W in A, where X is a junction head: narrow frame (p2 <= 3) with p3 odd (W read from p3; e.g. 'o' + Z-run, 'Z #', 'o #'), or p1 odd >= 5, or p1 = 3 with p2 odd (W read from p1). Phase(m, W) := next phase start (M', C') reached from 0^inf 0 A> (10)^m W 0^inf. k_align(C) := number of Incs until C is in A.

rules.name: Gap-Inc
rules.from: L A> S^(b+1) C, walls of C 0,p1,p2,.. with p1 in {1,2}
rules.to: L S A> S^b C', with p1 -> p1+1 (if it reaches p2 both walls vanish)
rules.cases: b>=1, any p2 (either parity); covers aligned d=1->2, d=2->3, width-2 'o' merges, 'o #', 'Z #', the carry into the zero tail

rules.name: J-rule (junction carry = one sub-phase)
rules.to: L S A> S^b [00 (10)^M' C'] with (M',C') = Phase(j-1, W); halts iff Phase(j-1, W) halts
rules.cases: j=1 is the round-1 d=3 carry (W = 0 (10)^e R) and also handles d=3 frames of odd width ('Z o #'); j>=2 is the renormalisation of shifted frames

validated.script: scripts/deepen2_validate_jrule.py seeds 1, 2 (j=1..12, b=1..30, aligned and wall-random W)
validated.mutation: Phase(j, W) instead of Phase(j-1, W): 187/200 fail
validated.orbit: 1702/1702 junction bounces (p1>=5) to 1e11, sub-phases replayed recursively

rules.name: Even head (halting)
rules.to: p1=4: HALT at once (B> Z -> # E>, E> Z -> F reads 1); p1>=6: odd-grid sub-run starting on a 1

rules.name: J-crossing (marker meets a frame with odd p1)
rules.to: 0^inf 0 L S A> [00 (10)^M' C'] with (M',C') = Phase(j-1, W), then A> o S -> # S A> (C3b) and the walk goes on
rules.cases: j=1 = round-1 C3a; j>=2 never met on the orbit (marker crossings there: d1 1338, d2 939, d3 1124, T 67)

rules.name: Round-1 aligned rules
rules.from: Inc (aligned), C1a, Z-absorb, C3a, C3b, C2, T

rules.name: Phase map (composition)
rules.to: C after M-1 Incs, then the marker walk -> next phase start (M', C')

closed_gaps: Eat closed for aligned counters: it is the marker walk continuing through the counter; 7 exact block rules (Inc, C1a, Z-absorb, C3a, C3b, C2, T) validated 1300/1300 each, with '#' walls in the left part (scripts/deepen_validate_walk.py; mutating C1a or C2 drops them to 0/1000).
Why g and the new counter do not depend on N: the walk only reads the counter; the bell just grows by the absorbed blocks.

Phase end is exact: C2/T give the left-record configuration; the new phase is 2 steps later, read one cell shifted, which explains the Z-runs and the 'pending' shapes (shifted frames: o Z^(e+1), o # Z^e, o S Z^e, terminator o S).
Phase-start grammar to 1e11 (1324 phases): 1071 match (o S+)* (o Z*) (shifted frame)* o S (C2 end), 102 match aligned frames + Z (T end), 61 have a third junction shape.

Junction invariant: an aligned frame 'o S' (one S) never sits directly before an empty junction (0 of 1324; k=2/3/4+ seen 69/17/145 times). This follows from C3b, which always leaves '# S A>'. Random counters that break it halt (37/3000).
Halting can come only from structure: 3000/3000 random aligned counters ran 8 phases with no halt, and every C1/C2/C3/T branch is non-halting whatever the digits.

Round 2: Inc on shifted frames closed. A shifted counter has a junction (odd first gap), and the first carry into it is exactly one full phase of the machine on the sub-counter: J-rule Inc(0 (10)^j W) = 00 (10)^M' C', (M',C') = Phase(j-1, W). Validated 1500/1500 random (incl. 157 halt-agree), 84/84 structured, 1702/1702 orbit junction bounces; mutation j-1 -> j fails 187/200. Example from round 1: o Z o Z o Z o S is 'o' + junction; the merge then the J-rule give o S6 o S2 Z.

Round 2: wall view. Counters are wall lists; for p1 in {1,2} Inc moves the first wall right and cancels coincident walls (Gap-Inc, 1500/1500, any parity of p2). This covers the width-2 'o' frames, 'o #', 'Z #' and the zero tail (the tail = endless width-2 'o' frames; terminator Z = frame (3, width 4)).

Round 2: marker crossing shifted frames / landing on a token closed. A frame with odd p1 (d=3 frame, odd-width 'Z o #', or junction) is crossed by the J-rule with b=0, then C3b (366/366 + 34 halt-agree). On the orbit the outer marker meets only d1/d2/d3/T frames; after the M-1 Incs the counter is fully aligned in 1320/1322 phases.

Round 2: third junction shape derived. 'o S2 Z #...' = aligned prefix + narrow frame 'Z #' (walls 0,2,3) + even run. Gap-Inc merges it into a junction with odd p1, then the J-rule. With the narrow heads 'o' and 'o #' and the heads 'J >= 5' and odd-width 'Z o #', every one of the 1324 phase starts parses as G1 (one junction, W aligned).

Round 2: complete regime coverage to 1e11. The bounce-level replay (bell removed) reproduces all 1321 phase starts 3..1323 exactly. Of ~6.94e6 Incs: Gap-Inc kinds d1 3466687, d2 3463754, o-merges 2390, 'o #' 58, 'Z #' 118, tail 334; J-rule kinds junction 1702 (j=2..34), odd-width d=3 332, overflow T 3277. Marker steps: d1 1338, d2 939, d3 1124, T 67, plus ~14.3k walk Incs of the same kinds. Sub-phases (recursive): aligned rules only. No even head (p1 >= 4 even) ever.

Round 2: why halting needs small M. Halting needs an even head (p1 = 4 halts at once) or a sub-phase on a non-aligned W; both need M-1 < k_align at some phase start. Orbit counters with M forced to <= k_align: 7 halts in 3293 (6 with M < k_align/3), 0 in 1100 with M in [3k/4, k]; with M > k_align: 0 in 2200 (8 phases each; deepen2_lowM.py + deepen_xrand.c).
remaining_gaps: Margin lemma (the one missing piece of a proof): M-1 >= k_align(C) at every phase start. It holds on the orbit from phase 8 to 1e11 with min ratio 1.4 (>= 2.4 after phase 68). It is not inductive by a constant factor on random G1 counters, so the proof must use orbit structure. Likely route: k_align ~ 2*3^(h_total), where h counts the d=1 prefix frames from '#' walls (= d=3 frames crossed by the previous walk) along the chain of J-rule outputs. On the orbit h is small (mean 1.0-1.2, max 6) while log3 M reaches 8.4; max 3^h/M per 250-phase window falls 0.58, 0.13, 0.04, 0.11, 0.03, 0.008.

Priority call for Dennis: is the margin structural or luck? Crude digit heuristic: each crossed digit is 2 with probability 1/3, so P(h >= k) ~ 2^-k. If digits were random, margin violations would be rare but not summable (about sum M^-0.63). Mild violations look harmless (0/1100 halts with M in [3k/4, k]). If the margin cannot be bounded structurally, the machine is a cryptid-margin case. The dynamics themselves need no pseudo-random arithmetic (counting + recursion).

Formal side not started: the aligned-walk lemma (Phase(m, A) in G1, non-halting) uses only round-1 rules + aligned Inc and can be formalized now; the J-rule needs a recursive (nested-phase) lemma in Rocq.

rounds.result: No margin proof. The strict margin M-1 >= k_align(C) is not inductive on random reachable-looking counters and depends on the exact bell (low base-3 digits of M-1-k_align). By the funded stage's exit rule (failed bound) the machine is parked as STUCK, cryptid-margin suspect. Not CRYPTID_CANDIDATE: no tested margin break led to halting.

rules.name: Aligned Inc = bijective base 3
rules.from: aligned counter, frames (d_i,w_i) below the top frame
rules.to: n incs add n to sum d_i 3^i (digits d in 1..3, widths fixed) until all lower digits are 3; the next inc carries into the top frame (cell level)

rules.name: Walk merges widths
rules.from: post-inc counter, marker walk crossing d=1/d=3 frames, stopping at d=2
rules.to: each '#' (D) frame of the next counter = merger of a crossed d=3 frame and the following d=1 frames, width = sum of their widths; d=1 frames before the first d=3 go into the bell (M' = M + 1 + sum w/2)
